skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Refines rough product or technical ideas into validated designs through focused questions, alternative comparison, and incremental review.
skill.summary: Guides idea exploration into a clear design before implementation begins.

content.value_statement: Early product and technical ideas often lack clear constraints, trade-offs, and success criteria. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through questions, options, and validated design sections.
actual_capabilities: Asks one clarifying question at a time to define purpose, constraints, and success criteria.
Compares two or three approaches with trade-offs and complexity.
Presents design sections in 200 to 300 word chunks for validation.
Uses decision matrix and design document templates for structured output.
Includes example sessions for authentication storage and real-time dashboard design.
limitations: It does not implement code or create an execution plan by itself.
It depends on user answers to resolve ambiguous requirements.
Its examples are guidance, not production-ready security or architecture advice.
It does not replace domain expert review for regulated systems.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify goals, constraints, and success measures before assigning implementation work.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Evaluate multiple architectures with trade-offs, costs, and complexity before coding.

use_cases.title: Document Design Decisions
use_cases.description: Turn a chosen direction into a structured design document and decision record.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help me refine this idea: [idea]. Ask one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to compare two or three approaches for [goal]. Show trade-offs before recommending a direction.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Design Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to turn our chosen approach into a design document with requirements, architecture, risks, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to challenge this proposed design: [design summary]. Identify missing constraints, alternatives, and revisit criteria.

output_examples.input: A founder wants to build a customer health dashboard.
output: Clarifying question about target users and decisions.
Three options: polling, server-sent updates, or streaming.
Validated design sections covering data flow, errors, and rollout.

output_examples.input: An engineer is choosing authentication storage.
output: Trade-off comparison for cookies, tokens, and server-side sessions.
Selected direction based on revocation, security, and infrastructure needs.
Security considerations for cookies, CSRF protection, and session expiry.

output_examples.input: A team needs a decision record for a search feature.
output: Weighted decision matrix with criteria and scores.
Clear rationale for the selected option.

best_practices: Start with the user goal and success criteria before discussing implementation.
Keep each question focused so the user can make one decision at a time.
Record rejected alternatives and revisit criteria in the final document.
anti_patterns: Skipping clarification and proposing a full architecture from a vague request.
Presenting many options without clear trade-offs or selection criteria.
Treating examples as final designs without adapting them to real constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It helps define a design before coding or task planning starts.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when an idea is vague, early, or has several viable approaches.

faq.question: What does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces clarified requirements, approach comparisons, validated design sections, and optional decision documents.

faq.question: Can it handle nontechnical ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. The questioning and trade-off method works for product, process, and planning decisions.

faq.question: Does it make final decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It presents options and asks the user to validate each major choice.
